newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France/Turkish Airlines to launch new service.
newsitem.headline: Air France/Turkish Airlines to launch new service.

text.p: Air France Cargo said it will launch a three-times weekly Boeing 727-200F feeder service, between Paris and Istanbul later this month in conjunction with Turkish Airlines.
The B727-200Fs, which are part of Turkish Airlines' fleet, have a freight capacity of approximately 20 tonnes.
Around 60 percent of the cargo carried on the flights is expected to be textiles manufactured in Turkey destined for the U.S. market, an Air France Cargo official told Reuters.
"The feeder service will be upgraded to five flights per week during the winter season which begins at the end of October, to meet expected demand," he said.

Air France is to suspend its weekly cargo stopover in Istanbul on the westbound leg of a scheduled 747-200F service from Karachi, with the launch of the new Istanbul-Paris freighter service, the official added.
Turkish Airlines currently operates 727-200F flights between Maastricht and Istanbul.
Air France and Turkish Airlines each operate twice daily passenger services between Paris and Istanbul.
